rationale: dual_domain_bilateral_n2i-claude-agentic: warm_start=True, pretrain_epochs=2, train_n=400, n_iter=120, val_n=200, batch_size=1, grad_clip=1.0, lr=0.005, proj_n_bf=1, img_n_bf=3, outer_wall_s=1050, seed=42, rationale=iter-2 dual_domain_bilateral_n2i, ONE-KNOB vs iter-1. PRIOR: iter-1 (img_n_bf=1, 6 params) hr=0.0, val_ssim=0.9567, val_psnr=38.44, recon_rmse 9.80e-4 slightly ABOVE baseline_rmse 9.65e-4 (recon marginally WORSE than the clean 128-view FBP -> hr floors at 0). This is the documented N2I-over-smooths-dense-breast failure (findings.md 2026-05-22). KNOB: image-domain BF DEPTH img_n_bf 1->3 (proj_n_bf held at 1). HYPOTHESIS: a deeper image-domain BF cascade (3 stacked TrainableBilateralFilter2d = 12 img params) gives the N2I loss more edge-preserving capacity, so it MIGHT recover fine detail rather than blur -- if hr climbs off 0, depth is a live lever; if it stays 0 (or SSIM/PSNR drop), deeper BF just compounds the over-smoothing and DEPTH is exhausted as an escape from the N2I ceiling. FAILURE MODE watched: over-smoothing (val_psnr drops below iter-1 38.44 / recon_rmse rises above baseline). BUDGET: img_n_bf 1->3 triples image-domain unfold cost but on breast's light 128-view adjoint iter-1 ran 1200s at depth1/n_iter120; depth3 image BF is cheap vs the FBP adjoints, expect <1300s; outer_wall_s=1050 internal backstop unchanged (it cut iter-1 at 195/200 scenes -> val_n effectively ~195, consistent across iters). ONE knob changed: img_n_bf 1->3.
